reason: Both conversations correctly refused the DIY regas up front, but Conversation 2 then reasoned from the symptoms the homeowner reported (no frost, rear wall not cold, compressor running non-stop, condenser barely warm) to a clear, honest conclusion that it's very likely a sealed-system fault, explained why gas alone won't fix it, and told him exactly what to say to a refrigeration engineer. Conversation 1 ignored the homeowner's volunteered R600a and knife-defrosting facts, ran through a rigid script of irrelevant checks (door ajar, holiday mode, vents, seals, condenser dust) despite him repeatedly supplying the decisive 'no frost, back wall not cold' evidence, and ended by repeating the same condenser-cleaning instruction verbatim without ever giving a diagnosis or escalation. Neither mentioned the uneconomic-repair/replacement angle, but 2 reached the right diagnosis and escalation efficiently while 1 never got there.
